seen.extent: Letter no. 780 (marked 'Duplicado') from London, 8 Sep 1837, 12 images. Cipher runs: 2 lines at top of image 3 plus a short group mid-page ('4607229' digits), a block of 7 lines on image 5, 3 lines at top of image 12, and one more run lower on image 12; several hundred letters in all.
seen.cipher: Monoalphabetic-looking letter substitution written in the same cursive hand as the Spanish text (letters g, h, l, n, p, u, v, y, z, o, c, e dominate), embedded in clear Spanish with a few digit groups for names. No decipherment, interlinear gloss or marginal plaintext on any leaf viewed.

2421.key_check: No key found or held for Azuares's cipher; nothing on DECODE or in the repo. The N.5 sheet (lead 2422) is a long enciphered text in a different notation (dotted letters struck through), not a key table, so it is not a key for this letter; untested.
2421.key_in_volume: None identified. Volume DIVERSOS-COLECCIONES 161 holds N.5 (Villafranca) with a cipher sheet that PARES says explains the key used; viewed, it is cipher text in a different script style and does not serve as a visible key for N.2. Untested against N.2.

Marked 'Duplicado' on the cover: another copy of no. 780 may exist elsewhere in the fonds; not found.

seen.extent: Enciphered sheet ('2o pliego') running over images 11 to about 20, 14 lines per page of roughly 30 dotted letters each, so well over 3000 letters in total; covering letters on images 1-10 in clear Spanish.
seen.cipher: Single Spanish letters (including ll and n-tilde) separated by dots, each letter struck through by a diagonal pen stroke: a letter-for-letter substitution, possibly with nulls, in 14-line pages. Images 11-16 viewed show no decipherment, plaintext or key table on or between the leaves.

seen.extent: Letter of 6 May 1840 on Ejercito de Cataluna, Brigada de Reserva letterhead. Image 2 holds five dot-separated number runs (about 120 numbers); image 3 carries one run of about 16 numbers before the signature.
seen.cipher: Numeric substitution with numbers 1-34 and 70 (70 recurs at the end of several runs, possibly a space or null; not tested), embedded in clear Spanish about Tarragona, Cervera, Solsona and Llacuna. No decipherment written on or with the leaves.
